name: IBPS RRB (Officer Scale I & Office Assistant)
tagline: Officer Scale I (PO) and Office Assistant (Multipurpose) jobs in Regional Rural Banks

overview.about: IBPS conducts the CRP-RRBs for Regional Rural Banks. Office Assistants are selected through Prelims and Mains (no interview); Officer Scale I candidates go through Prelims, Mains and an interview. Prelims has only Reasoning and Quant in 45 minutes, and Mains can be taken in English or Hindi.
eligibility: Graduation in any discipline (agriculture, horticulture, forestry, animal husbandry, veterinary, agri-engineering, pisciculture, agri-marketing, cooperation, IT, management, law, economics or accountancy are preferred for Officer Scale I)
Office Assistant: age 18–28 years; Officer Scale I: age 18–30 years; relaxation SC/ST 5 yrs, OBC-NCL 3 yrs, PwBD 10 yrs
Proficiency in the local language of the participating RRB

pattern.note: No separate sectional timing; −0.25 per wrong answer

pattern.paper: Prelims (both posts) — Quantitative Aptitude / Numerical Ability

pattern.note: Same structure for Officer Scale I and Office Assistant
Final = Mains 80 : Interview 20; Office Assistant merit is Mains only

Number system — divisibility, HCF & LCM, remainders, unit digits

chapters.title: Officer Scale I vs Office Assistant: pattern & strategy

cards.title: Two posts, one syllabus
cards.body: Both posts share the same subject list. **Office Assistant** (clerk): Prelims → Mains → language test, no interview. **Officer Scale I** (PO): Prelims → Mains → interview (80 : 20). You may apply for both; exams are held on different days.

cards.title: 45-minute composite Prelims
cards.body: Prelims has **only Reasoning and Quant**, 80 questions in **45 minutes** with no sectional timer. That is about **34 seconds per question**. You choose how to split time, so a tested plan is essential.

cards.title: Prelims plan
cards.body: Typical split: Reasoning 22–24 min, Quant 20–22 min. Start with your stronger section. In Reasoning, do inequality, syllogism, coding and direction before the big puzzles; in Quant, do simplification/approximation and series first.

cards.title: Mains: 200 questions in 120 minutes
cards.body: Mains is a composite **2-hour** paper with 200 questions, about 36 seconds each. Computer (40 Q for 20 marks) and GA can be done fast; save the rest of the time for Reasoning and Quant (50 marks each).

cards.title: Hindi option
cards.body: In Mains you can take the language section in **English or Hindi**. Pick the one in which you read faster and make fewer grammar mistakes. The question paper itself is bilingual for other sections.

cards.q: IBPS RRB Prelims has 80 questions in 45 minutes. Average time per question is closest to:
Which RRB post has an interview?
cards.explain: Officer Scale I has an interview (weighted 20%); Office Assistant selection is on Mains marks.

cards.q: The Computer Knowledge section in RRB Mains carries:
cards.explain: Computer Knowledge has 40 questions worth 20 marks (0.5 each).

notes.p: IBPS RRB recruits for **Office Assistant (Multipurpose)** (a clerical post) and **Officer Scale I** (an entry-level officer post) in Regional Rural Banks, along with Scale II and III officers. Both main posts share the same subjects, and you may apply for both; the exams are held on different days.
points: **Office Assistant:** Prelims → Mains → language proficiency test; **no interview**; merit on Mains.
**Officer Scale I:** Prelims → Mains → Interview; merit = Mains and interview in **80 : 20**.
Prelims for both: only **Reasoning and Quant**, 80 questions in 45 minutes.

notes.p:
Prelims has **80 questions (40 Reasoning + 40 Quant) in 45 minutes**, with **no sectional timer**. That works out to **2,700 seconds ÷ 80 ≈ 34 seconds per question**. Because you choose how to split the time, a **tested plan** is essential; there are sectional cut-offs as well as an overall cut-off, so neither section can be ignored.

**Worked example: building a time plan**
Total = 45 minutes. Suppose Reasoning is your stronger section.
Reasoning first: 22 minutes → aim for about 32–34 attempts.
Quant: 21 minutes → aim for about 28–30 attempts.
Buffer: 2 minutes to revisit marked questions.
22 + 21 + 2 = 45 ✓.
Re-test this split in at least 8–10 mocks and adjust by a minute or two.
Start with quick, predictable topics to bank marks early.
points: **Reasoning:** inequality, syllogism, coding–decoding, direction and blood relations first; then one or two puzzles.
**Quant:** simplification/approximation and number series first; then quadratic equations and arithmetic; leave DI for the end.
Mark and skip any question taking more than 60 seconds on the first pass.

notes.p:
Mains is a **single composite 2-hour paper** with **200 questions**, about **36 seconds each**. For Officer Scale I, the usual structure is Reasoning 40 Q (50 marks), Quant 40 Q (50 marks), General Awareness 40 Q (40 marks), English or Hindi 40 Q (40 marks) and Computer Knowledge 40 Q (20 marks). Check the latest notification for any change.

Computer (0.5 marks each) and GA are fast. A common plan: GA and Computer in about 25–30 minutes, then split the remaining time between Reasoning and Quant, which carry 50 marks each.
points: Language: choose **English or Hindi**, whichever you read faster and with fewer errors.
Negative marking applies; avoid blind guessing.
Practising Prelims with separate 20-minute timers (the real exam has none).
Spending 15 minutes on one puzzle in a 45-minute paper.
Ignoring GA because the Prelims has no GA section.
Not preparing rural banking topics that dominate RRB GA.
Office Assistant: no interview; merit on Mains.
Officer Scale I: Mains + interview (80 : 20).
Prelims: 80 Q in 45 min, ≈34 s per question, no sectional timer.
Mains: 200 Q in 120 min, ≈36 s per question.
Computer: 40 Q for 20 marks.
Language section: English or Hindi.

chapters.title: Rural banking awareness (RRBs, NABARD, KCC, PSL)

cards.title: RRB basics
cards.body: RRBs were set up from **2 October 1975** to serve small farmers, labourers and rural artisans; governed by the **RRB Act, 1976**. Ownership **Centre 50 : sponsor bank 35 : state 15**. **NABARD** supervises RRBs; RBI regulates them.

cards.title: Consolidation
cards.body: RRBs were merged in phases from 196 to 43, and under **'One State, One RRB'** (effective **1 May 2025**) to **28 RRBs**. The aim: stronger capital, technology and scale.

cards.title: NABARD
cards.body: Set up on **12 July 1982** on the recommendation of the **CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman) committee**. It refinances banks for agriculture and rural lending, manages the **RIDF**, and supervises RRBs and cooperative banks. HQ: Mumbai.

cards.title: Priority sector lending targets
points: Domestic SCBs: 40% of ANBC
Agriculture sub-target: 18% of ANBC
RRBs and small finance banks: 75% of ANBC
Shortfall goes to RIDF and similar funds

cards.title: Kisan Credit Card
cards.body: Introduced in **1998** (R.V. Gupta committee) for timely short-term crop credit. Under the interest subvention scheme, eligible farmers get loans at **7%**, falling to an effective **4%** with prompt repayment. Budget 2025-26 raised the subvention limit from ₹3 lakh to **₹5 lakh**.

cards.q: Which body supervises Regional Rural Banks?
cards.explain: RBI regulates RRBs, but supervision is delegated to NABARD.

cards.q: The priority sector lending target for RRBs is:
cards.explain: RRBs (like small finance banks) must lend 75% of ANBC to priority sectors.
NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982.

notes.p:
RRBs were created to provide credit to **small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, rural artisans and small entrepreneurs**. The first RRBs were set up on **2 October 1975** (Prathama Bank, Moradabad, was the first), following the Narasimham Working Group, and they are governed by the **RRB Act, 1976**.

Shareholding is **Central Government 50% : sponsor bank 35% : state government 15%**. The **RBI regulates** RRBs, while **NABARD supervises** them. After repeated mergers (from 196 RRBs to 43), 'One State, One RRB' consolidation took effect on **1 May 2025**, leaving **28 RRBs** with stronger capital, technology and scale.
**NABARD** was set up on **12 July 1982** on the recommendation of the **CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman) committee**, under the NABARD Act, 1981. Its head office is in **Mumbai**.
points: **Refinance:** provides funds to banks for agricultural and rural lending.
**RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund):** created in 1995-96; funds rural roads, irrigation and other state projects. Banks' priority-sector shortfalls are deposited here.
**Supervision:** RRBs and state/district cooperative banks.
**Development:** SHG–bank linkage (since 1992), watershed and tribal development, farmer producer organisations (FPOs).

notes.p: PSL makes banks lend a share of credit to sectors that might otherwise be under-served. Targets are measured as a percentage of **ANBC (Adjusted Net Bank Credit)** or credit equivalent of off-balance-sheet exposure, whichever is higher.
points: Domestic scheduled commercial banks: **40%** of ANBC; agriculture sub-target **18%**.
RRBs and small finance banks: **75%** of ANBC.
Categories include agriculture, MSMEs, export credit, education, housing, social infrastructure, renewable energy and weaker sections.
Shortfalls are placed in RIDF and similar funds at lower interest.
**PSLCs** (Priority Sector Lending Certificates) let banks trade over-achievement.

notes.p:
An RRB has ANBC of **₹2,000 crore**.
Required PSL = 75% of 2,000 = **₹1,500 crore**.
If its actual priority-sector lending is ₹1,380 crore, shortfall = 1,500 − 1,380 = **₹120 crore**.
For a commercial bank with the same ANBC: PSL target = 40% × 2,000 = ₹800 crore; agriculture sub-target = 18% × 2,000 = **₹360 crore**.

Introduced in **1998** (based on the R.V. Gupta committee), the KCC gives farmers **timely short-term credit** for crops, plus allied needs. It is now extended to animal husbandry and fisheries.

Under the **interest subvention scheme**, eligible farmers get short-term crop loans at **7%**, falling to an effective **4%** with prompt repayment (3% prompt repayment incentive). Budget 2025-26 announced a rise in the limit under the modified interest subvention scheme from ₹3 lakh to **₹5 lakh**. Check the latest notification for current rates and limits.

points: RBI **regulates** RRBs; NABARD **supervises** them.
RRB share 50 : 35 : 15 (Centre : sponsor : state).
PSL target 75% for RRBs, 40% for commercial banks.
NABARD set up in 1982, not 1975.
KCC launched in 1998, not 1982.
RRBs: 2 Oct 1975; RRB Act 1976; 28 RRBs after 1 May 2025.
NABARD: 12 July 1982; CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman); Mumbai.
PSL: 40% (agri 18%) for SCBs; 75% for RRBs and SFBs.
RIDF: 1995-96; PSL shortfall goes there.
KCC: 1998; 7% → effective 4% with prompt repayment.

chapters.title: Local language & Office Assistant provisional allotment

cards.title: Language proficiency
cards.body: Each RRB serves a specific state, so candidates must be proficient in that state's local language. For Office Assistants, a **language proficiency test** is held before final allotment; it is **qualifying**.

cards.title: Practise early
cards.body: Read local-language newspapers for 15 minutes daily and practise simple banking conversations. Many candidates lose their allotment here even after clearing Mains.

cards.title: Merit and allotment
cards.body: Office Assistant: **Mains marks only**, state-wise. Officer Scale I: Mains + interview at **80 : 20**. Allotment to an RRB depends on merit, vacancies and your preferences.

cards.title: Interview for Officer Scale I
cards.body: Expect rural-economy questions: KCC, crop seasons, PM-KISAN, self-help groups, priority sector lending and why you want to work in a rural branch. Know the RRB(s) of your state by name.

cards.q: For IBPS RRB Office Assistant, the local language test is:
cards.explain: It is a qualifying test held before final allotment.

cards.q: Final merit for RRB Officer Scale I uses Mains and interview in the ratio:

notes.h: Why local language matters in RRBs
notes.p:
Each RRB serves a particular state, mainly in rural and semi-urban areas. Customers are farmers, labourers, self-help groups and small traders who often speak only the local language. That is why proficiency in the **local language of the state/RRB** is required.

For **Office Assistants**, a **language proficiency test** is held before final allotment, and it is **qualifying**. Officer Scale I candidates also need to be proficient in the local language; check the notification for how it is assessed.
How the final list is made differs by post.
points: **Office Assistant:** Mains marks only, **state-wise**; then provisional allotment and the language test.
**Officer Scale I:** Mains and interview combined **80 : 20**.
Allotment to a particular RRB depends on merit, vacancies, category and your preferences.
Many candidates lose an allotment at the language stage even after a good Mains score.

notes.h: Worked example: Officer Scale I final score
notes.p:
Assume Mains is scored out of 200 and the interview out of 100.
Candidate: Mains 120/200, Interview 70/100.
Mains part = 120 ÷ 200 × 80 = 0.6 × 80 = **48**.
Interview part = 70 ÷ 100 × 20 = **14**.
Final = **62/100**.
Compare a candidate with Mains 130 and interview 45: 0.65 × 80 = 52; 0.45 × 20 = 9; total **61**. Mains still carries more weight, but a good interview can close a gap of 10 Mains marks.

notes.h: Preparing for the Officer Scale I interview
notes.p: Expect questions rooted in the rural economy and the RRB's role.
points: Kisan Credit Card, interest subvention, crop insurance (PMFBY), PM-KISAN.
Crop seasons (kharif, rabi, zaid) and main crops of your state.
Self-help groups and SHG–bank linkage; priority sector lending.
The name and sponsor bank of your state's RRB.
Why you want to work in a rural branch, and how you would explain a loan to a first-time borrower.

notes.p:
Read a local-language newspaper for 15 minutes daily from the time you apply, not after Mains. Practise simple banking conversations: opening a Jan Dhan account, applying for a KCC, depositing cash, checking a passbook. Learn local words for crop loan, interest, instalment, collateral and insurance.

If the state's script is new to you, learn it first: spend the first two weeks on reading and writing the alphabet and common words, then move to short sentences. Write a short daily diary entry of 4–5 lines in the language and ask a fluent speaker to correct it once a week.

points: Language test for Office Assistants: qualifying, before final allotment.
Office Assistant merit: Mains only, state-wise.
Officer Scale I merit: Mains 80 : Interview 20.
Know your state's RRB and sponsor bank.
Prepare KCC, PMFBY, PM-KISAN, SHGs, PSL for the interview.
Start language practice early.
